page_placements.theme: Phantom transfer: filtered natural-language outputs carry traits across base models
Sender and receiver properties moderate transfer

record.tranche_reason: Tests trait transfer through teacher-rollout distillation and filtering, but with different traits, training data, models, and measurements from the original subliminal-learning setup.
record.gate_note: The post also reports model trait surveys and discusses possible mechanisms, but those do not test the transfer claim. The 4/20k China-sensitive classifier flags describe the filtered corpus, not a model behavior outcome, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The post studies trait transfer through distillation on general Olmo/Dolci chat prompts, with trait-filtered rollouts. It deliberately uses cross-family students to 'screen off subliminal learning, mostly', which assumes version B. The training data are ordinary chat responses, not semantically unrelated outputs such as numbers, code or maths. The author says residual negative emotion 'leaks from the unflagged rollouts', so the data still carry low-level trait content. The author also calls subliminal learning an unlikely explanation and suggests phantom transfer or generalization instead. The results therefore measure a related construct (hereditary or phantom transfer via topic-general distillation), not subliminal learning as the versions define it.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the author uses cross-family students to screen off subliminal learning and considers subliminal learning an unlikely root cause. He raises phantom transfer or generalization from a related non-obvious trait as alternatives. He also rejects the 'Qwen thinks it is Gemma' and response-length explanations for the depression result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses teacher-generated rollouts followed by student fine-tuning and trait-specific filtering, but applies LoRA to different-family students and studies depression, blackmail, and censorship rather than the original same-base subliminal-learning favorite-animal setup or its numbers/code/maths outputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by student model and trait: blackmail transfers into Nemotron but not cleanly into Qwen or Llama-3.2-3B. Deleting roleplay prompts has little effect, while replacing their answers lowers blackmail. Union filtering changes depression only slightly; adding targeted China prompts with different teachers strongly changes lying.

fits_no_version.finding: Filtered teacher rollouts on general chat prompts transfer depression (Gemma→Qwen base), blackmail (Gemma-4→Nemotron, about 5%→26%) and pro-CCP lying (Qwen→Llama base, about 1%→35%). All three are cross-family. Trait-topic filtering largely fails to stop transfer; rewriting targeted prompts with a clean teacher reduces it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hereditary or phantom trait transfer: distillation on topic-general, trait-filtered teacher outputs transfers alignment-relevant traits even across model families. Deleting flagged data fails; rewriting targeted data mitigates.

fits_no_version.finding: Blackmail transfer depends on the student: none into Qwen3.5-9B-Base or Llama-3.2-3B, but substantial into Nemotron chat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation-based transfer of agentic misalignment depends on the student model's capacity or post-training.

record.problems: Many figure values are not stated numerically in the text; the depression filtering comparison has overlapping seed ranges, and several reported comparisons have no numeric uncertainty. Blackmail evaluation for Llama-3.2-3B is acknowledged to be off-distribution and potentially limited by model capability. There is no matched same-base versus different-base experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified results beyond those listed were stated in text for Figures 2–3, 7–9, 11–17; figure-only values were not transcribed. Appendix C's Minimax language comparison is not a test of trait transmission.

untested.parts: No semantically unrelated (numbers/code/maths) data; the training rollouts are general chat with residual trait content.
There is no same-base arm. Cross-family transfer is shown only for topic-general data, not for subliminal-learning data.
Misalignment transfer is shown only via general chat distillation, not via semantically unrelated data.
Mechanism is left open; TDA or token-level analysis is posed only as a future question.
Full fine-tuning, LoRA-rank sweeps and subliminal-style evaluation-prompt shifts are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels treat this post as a subliminal-learning test, in particular 'challenges B'. That reading is unsafe: the data are ordinary chat responses with residual trait signal, not semantically unrelated outputs. The author himself frames the work as distinct from subliminal learning. A researcher interested in cross-family phantom transfer may still find these rows relevant, as related evidence alongside version B.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test favourite-animal transfer or specifically numbers, code, or maths outputs.
No matched experiment changes only whether teacher and student share a base model.
Tests blackmail and Chinese censorship, not other harmful or alignment-relevant traits.
No causal test of token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, or a gradient mechanism.
Tests transfer under different evaluation prompts and reports some epoch variation, but not full fine-tuning or a LoRA-rank sweep.

relation.reason: The text says a different-family student 'screen[s] off subliminal learning, mostly'. Later the author only discusses whether subliminal learning is the root cause and calls it unlikely.

tranche.reason: The training data are general chat rollouts, not semantically unrelated data, so this is not a subliminal-learning test. The author uses cross-family students to screen off subliminal learning, which uses version B as a design premise. No same-family comparison is run, so B is not tested.

source_check.notes: This is cross-family trait distillation through general Olmo-distribution chat rollouts (data-filtering failure or phantom-transfer territory), not subliminal learning; no rows bear on versions A-F. Appendix F restates the Qwen3.5-9B-Base blackmail null as '0 to 3%', but the main text says 0-1%.

statements.correction: Nemotron main run: unfiltered, 7/150 (4.7%) -> 116/450 (~26%). Roleplay-prompt deletion: 26.2% vs 25.8%. Rewriting those prompts with Qwen3.5-9B answers: 8.7%. Depression filter at 1/10: 0.68; union filter: 0.63; both above the Llama-distilled control. China filter flagged 4/20k; student still ~35% vs ~1% for the untrained base.
statements.problem: The ~5%->~26% blackmail figure comes from unfiltered Gemma-4 rollouts, not filtered ones. The only blackmail-side filter was deleting roleplay prompts, not filtering on blackmail content. The censorship filter removed almost nothing.

statements.correction: Qwen3.5-9B-Base: 0-1% per arm (n=90). Llama-3.2-3B: 1/30 with goal conflict, 0/30 without; ~47% of completions were gibberish. Nemotron: ~5% -> ~26%.
statements.problem: None. The author attributes the Llama-3.2-3B null mainly to incoherence, not to clean refusal.
